checks.invariant: A delegated hunter or tool lane receives only the authority its contract grants (writes only its own agents/<agent-id>/inputs/ folder, or its own reports), and the verdict's inputs cannot be written by a delegated task.
checks.result: The narrowing exists only as prose. The contract (agents/vulnerability-hunter.md:38-44), overlay item 4 and lane-secrets.md:25 say a subagent writes almost nothing. The hunt guardrail judges the write path against the session, not the agent. Any file tool call in the session may write anywhere under reviews/<ID>/ (hooks/qa-guardrail:904-912). Only .ultrapowers/(runs|sandbox) and the protected-path list are refused. hunt-verdict.mjs takes the highest run-<N> folder (:192-211) and trusts findings.json, coverage-ledger.json, tool-lanes.json and research.json by shape (:254-306). Nothing binds the loaded run to the run record or to the preflight's RUN folder. A prompt-injected delegated agent therefore holds write authority over the verdict's inputs. Recorded as candidate hunt-contract:subagent-write-scope-reaches-verdict-inputs. Fake sandbox artifacts are not reachable, because verify matches the protected sandbox log.

checks.invariant: Tool-lane, verifier and research prompts treat tree, tool and web text as data and carry no secret or tracker authority beyond the contract's listed tools; the research step (unguarded, session tools) gets only sanitized rows.
checks.result: Every prompt states that tree, page and tool text are data and that the lanes never dispatch subagents. The OSINT and secrets lanes forbid copying secret fields. The research step is given only the preflight's DECLARED rows (the code-side filter is h3's). research.md is unchanged in range. The advisory verifier receives the research row unchanged. That row carries web-derived free text in `conditions` and `reason`, but the verifier can only confirm or downgrade, and it runs under the guardrail. Nothing further to report beyond the hardening notes.

checks.invariant: The changed files hold no hardcoded credentials, security TODO/FIXME markers, ungated debug switches, seeded credentials, committed key files, dynamic-code sinks or permissive scaffold defaults.
checks.result: I grepped the added lines of the full range, excluding the vendored folder. Hits for secret-shaped strings are all dummy test inputs for the redaction and gitleaks tests (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE, runtime-assembled AKIA/ghp_/xoxb- strings, `s3cretvalue`, a fake RSA block, ghp_SECRETTOKEN in a preflight fixture). The hunt-guardrail cases use evil.example.net URLs as deny cases. No TODO, FIXME, HACK or XXX appears. No new process.env or ULTRAPOWERS_ debug switch appears in hooks or hunt scripts. No .env, .pem, .key or credential file is added; the added files are only docs, tests, scripts, prompts and the vendored folder. There is no HTTP, CORS, cookie or redirect surface. eval, new Function and dynamic import() do not occur. child_process use is spawn/spawnSync with argument arrays and no shell:true (hunt-sandbox.mjs, tests). The vendored validators require only fs, path and util, with no process.env, network or child_process. Template defaults changed to hunt.depth {ticket: quick, full: standard}, and the sandbox is opt-in with digest-pinned images. The package.json dependency set is unchanged (zero dependencies). The vendored folder is for the secrets lane (gitleaks found none) and the dependencies lane.

checks.invariant: Each vendored Cloudflare file's committed bytes match the byte count and SHA-256 in PROVENANCE.md; the loaded validators are the vendored ones, with no line-ending rewrite and no extra or unlisted file.
checks.result: I ran sha256sum and wc -c over all 21 vendored files in the working tree. Every hash and byte count equals its PROVENANCE.md row. I also hashed the committed blobs on the branch for the validators, report-schema.json, SECURITY-AUDIT.md and HUNTING.md, and they match too. The folder holds 22 tracked files (21 plus PROVENANCE.md), all regular mode 100644. .gitattributes pins the folder `-text`, so no EOL conversion alters the bytes. test-vendored.mjs asserts size and hash, the exact file set, the table rows and the absence of any second SKILL.md, and run-tests.sh runs it. hunt-verdict.mjs requires the two validators by a relative path inside the plugin (:27-28) and reads the schema from the same folder (:125). Both validators import only fs, path and util. I did not run the vendored validators or their tests. The upstream bytes at the commit named in PROVENANCE.md cannot be fetched offline, so equality with upstream is unverified. A hash table that changes in the same commit as the files it lists is a record, not an independent root of trust. See the hardening notes.

candidates.title: A delegated hunt agent can write the verdict's inputs, because the write confinement is per run and the per-agent write scope is prose only
candidates.description: The hunt contract says subagents write almost nothing (a hunter only its own agents/<agent-id>/inputs/, the secrets lane only its gitleaks reports), and that the coordinator alone writes research.json, tool-lanes.json and the Cloudflare shared files. The guardrail enforces only the run's write area, reviews/<ID>/ plus .ultrapowers/ excluding runs and sandbox, for every tool call in the session, subagents included. The verdict script then reads the highest-numbered run-<N> folder and trusts findings.json, coverage-ledger.json, tool-lanes.json and research.json by shape, with no binding to the run record, the preflight's RUN folder or the file's author. A hunter or lane agent that reads the audited tree and is steered by text in it keeps a Write tool, and so holds authority over the files that decide SECURITY-REPORT.md and TASK-REVIEW.md. Examples are a higher run-N folder with forged records, or an overwritten tool-lanes.json that hides a secret or CVE row. The chain needs a prompt-injected delegated agent plus a forged set of records that Cloudflare's two validators accept. Injection alone is not the claim.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The delegation gives each hunter, lane and verifier agent the whole session toolset and the whole run write area, and narrows it only in prose: agents/vulnerability-hunter.md:38-44, the overlay's item 4 and the lane prompts. The deterministic check (hooks/qa-guardrail:904-912) cannot tell which agent wrote, and hunt-verdict.mjs trusts file shape instead of an owner or a binding to the live run.

trace.description: Hunters and lanes read the untrusted tree and are told only by prose to write nothing but their own inputs/ folder. They are dispatched with the session's tools, including Write.

A Write or Edit by any call of the session is allowed for any path under reviews/<ID>/, so findings.json, tool-lanes.json, research.json and a new run-<N>/ folder are all permitted. Only the protected-path list and .ultrapowers/(runs|sandbox) are refused.
The run used for the verdict is the highest run-<N> directory under reviews/<ID>/, not the run the preflight announced or the run record names.

findings, ledger, tool-lanes and research are accepted if they pass shape and Cloudflare's validator checks. No owner or origin is checked, so forged records reach the verdict, the front page and assemble-review.

evidence.description: Subagents write almost nothing: only the coordinator's own listed files and a hunter's own inputs/; no mechanism beyond the prose is named.
The reports under <RUN>/ are the only files this lane creates: a prompt-level rule.
The deny message names the limit as reviews/<id>/ and .ultrapowers/, which is the per-run scope, not a per-agent scope.
tool-lanes.json is accepted when it is shaped as a lanes object; there is no author or provenance check for it, for findings or for research.

blockers: The sandbox is unavailable for this run, and no target code or local check was run, so no forged run folder has been observed to be accepted by hunt-verdict.mjs.
Whether Cloudflare's validators accept a minimal forged ledger and findings set, and whether a harness delivers PreToolUse events for subagent calls, are facts observed at run time.
Whether the harness lets the coordinator's later writes overwrite a forged file is run-time ordering.

validation_plan.local: In a throwaway fixture repository with a dummy ticket, as a sandboxed or unit-test harness step: write a higher run-<N> folder holding a minimal valid run-metadata.json (run_status complete), coverage-ledger.json and findings.json through the hook's hunt profile as a subagent-origin event. Then run hunt-verdict.mjs verdict on it and check that it prints PASS for the forged run, not for the real run. The same hook-level case can be added to tests/qa-gatekeeper/fixtures/hunt/cases.json.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner can observe on Claude Code whether a hunter subagent's Write call to reviews/<ID>/run-<N+1>/findings.json is delivered to the hunt hook and allowed. If it is, per-agent confinement is absent in practice.

hardening: Remediation direction for the candidate: have the coordinator pass the run folder to the verdict script and compare it with the run record, so latestRun cannot pick a folder an agent created. Or add a coordinator-written manifest of file hashes that the verdict checks. Deny hunter and lane writes to anything outside agents/<agent-id>/ and their gitleaks reports, if the harness gives the agent identity to the hook.

hooks/qa-guardrail:790-799: the hunt profile lets tracker and mail MCP reads pass (gmail, slack, outlook, teams, jira, linear, odoo and the like), while the contract says the hunt uses no third-party service. A prompt-injected hunter with such a connector installed could read it and write the result into the reviews/<ID>/ files that are committed or posted by --post. This block is unchanged in range (the same lines exist on dev) and the guardrail is h1's, so it is a note. Narrowing to the tracker the project configured would honor the contract.

Contract line 138-149 and the SKILL.md rule say a harness without a guardrail keeps every Absolute rule. Those rules are prose-only there, and hunters read untrusted trees with the whole session toolset. This is an accepted design limit; the report states `Guardrail: not active`.

STEP 0b (research.md, unchanged in range) runs before the run record with session tools and no guardrail, reading public pages. The only project input is the preflight's DECLARED rows (h3). Its returned rows are written to research.json as returned, and the advisory verifier receives a row with web-derived free text unchanged. The verifier can only confirm or downgrade, and it runs under the guardrail. Treating the `conditions` and `reason` fields as data in the verifier prompt is already stated.

Vendored provenance: PROVENANCE.md, the EXPECTED table in test-vendored.mjs and the files are changed together in one change, and nothing at run time re-checks the hash before hunt-verdict.mjs requires the validators in-process. The only check is the CI test, which compares the repository with itself. Upstream equality at c1c8a8c1471069fb0e188eeaff69b8e8db6564a8 could not be checked offline. When the plugin is run from a checkout of a branch that is itself under audit, as for this repository, an edit to a vendored validator would execute in the verdict script; CI catches it only if the test runs on that branch. Pinning the commit hash through a signed tag or a second, independent record would give an independent root of trust. This is not a source-grounded exploit.

Test fixtures contain secret-shaped strings (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE, an RSA PRIVATE KEY marker, `s3cretvalue`). They are dummy and assembled or documented examples. A future gitleaks run over the whole tree will report them as rows unless the project's .gitleaks.toml allow-lists tests/vulnerability-hunt.
